---
title: "Case 31 Member Survey Dashboard"
description: "A descriptive dashboard showcasing the Case 31 SPSS survey data."
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    scrolling: true
    theme: [cosmo, styles.scss]
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

case31 <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_1.sav")

service_labels <- c(
  q3 = "Courteous",
  q4 = "Helpful",
  q5 = "Professional",
  q6 = "Available"
)

service_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(service_labels), function(variable) {
  tibble(
    dimension = unname(service_labels[[variable]]),
    score = as.numeric(case31[[variable]])
  )
})) |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  group_by(dimension) |>
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score),
    responses = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

perception_labels <- c(
  q30 = "Rates are lower",
  q31 = "Confidential",
  q32 = "Prompt",
  q33 = "Meets member needs",
  q34 = "Loan applications are simple"
)

perception_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(perception_labels), function(variable) {
  tibble(
    dimension = unname(perception_labels[[variable]]),
    score = as.numeric(case31[[variable]])
  )
})) |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  group_by(dimension) |>
  summarise(mean_score = mean(score), .groups = "drop")

overall_code <- as.numeric(case31$q37)
overall_labels <- c("Excellent", "Good", "Average", "Poor", "Very Poor", "No opinion")
overall_summary <- tibble(
  rating = factor(overall_code, levels = 1:6, labels = overall_labels)
) |>
  count(rating, .drop = FALSE)

valid_overall <- !is.na(overall_code) & overall_code %in% 1:5
positive_share <- mean(overall_code[valid_overall] %in% c(1, 2))

product_labels <- c(
  q13 = "Regular share account",
  q14 = "Special subaccounts",
  q15 = "Christmas club account",
  q16 = "IRA",
  q17 = "Master credit card",
  q18 = "Signature loans",
  q19 = "New car loans",
  q20 = "Late-model car loans",
  q21 = "Older-model car loans",
  q22 = "Household-goods loans",
  q23 = "Recreational loans",
  q24 = "Share-collateralized loan",
  q25 = "IRA loans",
  q26 = "Line-of-credit loans"
)

product_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(product_labels), function(variable) {
  values <- as.numeric(case31[[variable]])
  valid <- !is.na(values) & values %in% c(1, 2)
  tibble(
    product = unname(product_labels[[variable]]),
    used_rate = if (sum(valid) > 0) mean(values[valid] == 1) else NA_real_,
    valid_responses = sum(valid)
  )
})) |>
  filter(!is.na(used_rate)) |>
  arrange(desc(used_rate))

employee_mean <- mean(case31$OverallEmployeePerformace, na.rm = TRUE)
top_service <- service_summary$dimension[which.max(service_summary$mean_score)]
top_product <- product_summary$product[1]
top_product_rate <- product_summary$used_rate[1]
```

## Row {height="180px"}

### Survey responses

::: {.metric}
```{r, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("<strong>%s</strong>survey records", comma(nrow(case31))))
```
:::

### Employee service average

::: {.metric}
```{r, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("<strong>%.2f / 5</strong>across four service dimensions", employee_mean))
```
:::

### Positive overall rating

::: {.metric}
```{r, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("<strong>%s</strong>Excellent or Good", percent(positive_share, accuracy = 0.1)))
```
:::

### Data source

::: {.metric}
```{r, results="asis"}
cat("<strong>Case 31</strong>SPSS survey file")
```
:::

## Row

### Employee service dimensions

```{r}
ggplot(service_summary, aes(x = mean_score, y = reorder(dimension, mean_score))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0f766e", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_score)), hjust = -0.15, color = "#243b53") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 5.3), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(x = "Mean response (1–5)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Overall rating distribution

```{r}
ggplot(overall_summary, aes(x = rating, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a9d8f", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.35, color = "#243b53") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Responses") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

## Row

### Credit-union perceptions

```{r}
ggplot(perception_summary, aes(x = mean_score, y = reorder(dimension, mean_score))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#457b9d", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_score)), hjust = -0.15, color = "#243b53") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 5.3), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(x = "Mean agreement (1–5)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Product awareness and use

```{r}
product_plot <- product_summary |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(product = reorder(product, used_rate))

ggplot(product_plot, aes(x = used_rate, y = product)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#e76f51", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(used_rate, accuracy = 1)), hjust = -0.15, color = "#243b53") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1.08), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Used among valid responses", y = "Top 10 products by use rate") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Row

### What stands out

- The strongest employee-service dimension was **`r top_service`**, based on its mean rating.
- Among valid overall-rating responses, **`r percent(positive_share, accuracy = 0.1)`** were rated Excellent or Good.
- The most-used product in the available awareness/use variables was **`r top_product`**, used by **`r percent(top_product_rate, accuracy = 1)`** of valid responses.

### Interpretation and limitations

- This page provides descriptive summaries of **128 Case 31 survey records**; it does not display individual responses.
- Ratings use the scales supplied in the SPSS file. Higher mean scores indicate more favorable responses for the employee-service and credit-union-perception items.
- Product use rates are calculated only among valid responses coded as “Aware and Have Used” or “Aware but Have Not Used.”
- The dashboard describes this sample and should not be generalized to all members without information about the sampling design, response rate, and population.
- The source file contains additional variables that are not all shown here, including loan status, headquarters status, and statement-related questions.

::: {.callout-note}
The source file is `Case 31 Data_efcu_1.sav`. The dashboard uses aggregated results for demonstration and portfolio presentation. It does not claim to represent Avenue Shabu customer data or the Avenue Shabu culminating-experience project.
:::
